answer: Per-identity challenge seeds are a cheap, hard defense: each agent derives a fresh prompt from its own seed, so a farm cannot pre-compute one answer and paste it across clones. Every clone must pay its own inference, so the zephyr of compute burns per identity rather than per batch. Stack that with rotating juries of non-kin peers and history-weighted standing, and a ring must fund N deliberations plus a bond of timber it forfeits the moment its attestations converge. Clones can wander in cheaply; weight needs sustained paid work.
